record.field: Audit checklist for verifying security guard licensing and training as per SIRA (Dubai) regulations.
Guard has completed 40 hours of basic training
Guard has valid Medical Fitness Certificate
Guard is registered in SIRA system
UAE Security Guard Uniform & Appearance Audit
Audit checklist for verifying security guard uniform and grooming standards as per UAE regulations (SIRA/ASSD).
SIRA Badge visible on left chest/shoulder
Name tag clearly visible with guard/company name
Black safety shoes polished and in good condition
Personal grooming (hair, nails, facial hair) standards met
Equipment (flashlight, radio) carried in approved pouches
Audit checklist for verifying security guard readiness for emergency situations as per UAE protocols.
Guard knows nearest Fire Alarm Call Point location
Guard knows PASS method for fire extinguishers
Guard knows location of first aid kits
Guard knows site evacuation route and assembly point
CCTV & Control Room Operations Compliance Audit (SIRA)
Audit checklist for verifying CCTV operations and control room standards as per SIRA regulations.
CRO has valid SIRA Control Room Operator permit
Retention period meets SIRA standards (minimum 31 days)
All cameras are functional and properly positioned
Control room access is restricted to authorized personnel
System time is synchronized with UAE standard time
UAE Labor Law & Guard Welfare Compliance Audit
Audit checklist for verifying compliance with UAE Labor Law and guard welfare standards.
Guard has written employment contract in Arabic
Working hours comply with UAE Labor Law (max 8h/day, 48h/week)
Overtime is properly recorded and compensated
Guard has valid medical insurance card
Passport is in guard's possession (not held by employer)
Salary paid via WPS (Wage Protection System) by 10th of month
UAE Summer & Heat Stress Protocol Audit
Mandatory audit for summer months to ensure compliance with UAE heat stress and midday break regulations.
Midday break (12:30 PM - 3:00 PM) strictly observed for outdoor posts
Cool drinking water available for all guards at all times
Shaded rest areas provided for guards during breaks
Guards trained in recognizing signs of heat exhaustion/stroke
Electrolyte supplements/salts available in first aid kits
Audit for access control points and vehicle entry/exit procedures.
All vehicles log entry/exit time and plate number
Driver's ID (Emirates ID/Driving License) checked and recorded
Audit for master keys, restricted areas, and high-value asset protection.
Key register is up-to-date and accurate
All master keys are secured in a locked cabinet
Keys issued only to authorized personnel with signature
Audit for the quality, accuracy, and completeness of security logs and reports.
Daily Activity Reports (DAR) completed for every shift
Entries are legible, chronological, and in English
Incident reports are detailed with photos and evidence
Audit specifically for night shift performance and perimeter integrity.
Guards remain alert and awake throughout shift
Hourly perimeter patrols verified via NFC/QR scanners
Flashlights are operational and used during patrols
Audit for residential towers, villas, and gated communities.
Swimming pool and gym security rules enforced
Audit for mall environments, including crowd control and anti-shoplifting.
High-visibility patrols maintained in crowded areas
Audit for hotel security standards, DTCM compliance, and guest safety.
Audit for radio usage, code words, and reporting discipline.
Standard radio codes and terminology used correctly
Audit for first aid kit readiness and medical emergency preparedness.
First aid kits are fully stocked and no items are expired
Comprehensive audit for fire safety systems and prevention measures.
All fire extinguishers are in place and inspected monthly
Audit for lost and found inventory and handover protocols.
All items are correctly tagged and logged with photos
Audit for verifying visitor and contractor identification and site rules.
Visitors issued temporary badges and recorded in system
Audit for the completeness of shift handovers and post briefings.
Handover log signed by both outgoing and incoming guards
Audit for guard accommodation (if on-site) and guard post cleanliness.
Guard post is clean and free of personal items/food
Audit for temporary events, festivals, and large crowd scenarios.
Crowd control barriers in place as per site plan
Specific audit for schools and universities covering student safety and KHDA/ADEK requirements.
Student pickup/drop-off areas are properly supervised
Audit for medical facilities focusing on patient safety and DHA/DOH regulations.
Emergency room and ambulance access kept clear 24/7
Audit for heavy industry and construction sites covering PPE and material control.
All personnel on site wearing mandatory PPE (Helmet, Vest, Shoes)
Audit for executive protection and high-profile security details.
Close protection officer has valid SIRA CPO permit
Audit for CIT operations based on SIRA CIT regulations.
CIT armored vehicle is SIRA-approved and GPS-tracked
Detailed inspection of individual guard equipment readiness.
Radio, Flashlight, Baton, and Handcuffs (if authorized) in good condition
CCTV Control Room Health & Safety Audit
Audit focusing on the working environment and safety of control room operators.
Ergonomic seating and proper workstation lighting provided
Audit for measuring response times and patrol coverage efficiency.
Average response time to alarms is within SLA limits
Mobile Patrol Vehicle Safety & Equipment Audit
Audit for patrol vehicles, including safety equipment and branding.
Vehicle has mandatory fire extinguisher and first aid kit
Internal audit for physical fitness and mental readiness of guards.
Guard meets internal physical fitness requirements
Data Center & Critical Infrastructure Security Audit
High-security audit for data centers and essential infrastructure sites.
Dual-factor authentication used for all server room entries
Audit for parking security, illegal parking enforcement, and traffic flow.
Illegal parking in disabled or fire access zones reported/fined
Audit for warehouse loading bays and goods-in/out security.
Seal numbers on incoming/outgoing trucks verified and logged
Audit for minimizing retail shrinkage and preventing internal theft.
Staff lockers and bags checked during exit (if authorized by policy)
Audit for ensuring all electronic security systems are tested regularly.
Weekly testing of panic buttons and silent alarms recorded
Audit for evaluating guard and occupant performance during emergency drills.
Total evacuation time is within target limits
Audit for off-site guard accommodation as per UAE labor camp standards.
Accommodation meets MOHRE standards for space, ventilation, and hygiene
Audit for ensuring clients receive timely and accurate reports via portal.
All incident reports shared with client within 2 hours of occurrence
Audit for ensuring annual security risk assessments are conducted and updated.
Formal Security Risk Assessment (SRA) updated in the last 12 months
